Action Plan:
1. Obtain mid-stream urine (MSU) sample today for dipstick, microscopy, culture & sensitivity; patient to deliver sample to practice as instructed.  
2. Commence empiric antibiotic for presumed uncomplicated cystitis – Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (dose/route/frequency not documented) or, if unavailable/intolerant, Trimethoprim (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
3. Advise generous oral hydration and use of simple analgesia (Paracetamol, dose/frequency not documented) for suprapubic discomfort.  
4. Safety-net: seek urgent review if fever, flank/back pain, vomiting, frank hematuria, or lack of improvement within 7 days.  
5. Lifestyle counselling given regarding avoidance of cannabis use; brief alcohol advice provided.  
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Presenting with 5–7 day history of dysuria, increased urinary frequency, and dull aching suprapubic pain, worst during micturition.  
• Noted pink-tinged urine for first time today.  
• Denies loin pain, radiation, nausea, vomiting, or fever.  
• Bowel habit long-standingly variable (self-reported IBS); no new gastrointestinal symptoms.  
• Menstrual history: last period 2 weeks ago; uses combined oral contraceptive pill; last unprotected intercourse ~1 week ago.  
• Past medical history: Irritable Bowel Syndrome.  
• Surgical history: none reported.  
• Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (name/dose not documented); Mebeverine (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Clindamycin – adverse reaction (details not documented).  
• Social: 19-year-old university student (English), lives in halls with flatmate. Occasional alcohol; first-time cannabis use 1.5 weeks ago; non-smoker.  
• Family history: no bladder or kidney disease.

Objective:
• No physical examination performed (telehealth).  
• Vitals not recorded.  
• No investigations completed yet; MSU planned.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dysuria / Increased urinary frequency / Suprapubic pain  
   – Likely diagnosis: Uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (acute cystitis).  
   – Differential: Chlamydial urethritis, pregnancy, urolithiasis, early pyelonephritis.  
   – Investigations: MSU dipstick, microscopy, culture & sensitivity. Consider pregnancy test if symptoms persist or new concerns arise.  
   – Treatment: Empiric Nitrofurantoin 3-day course (dose/route/frequency not documented) OR Trimethoprim alternative; encourage fluids; Paracetamol for pain.  
   – Referrals: none at this stage.

2. Hematuria (pink urine)  
   – Assessment: Likely secondary to cystitis; monitor resolution with treatment.  
   – Investigations: Same MSU; repeat urinalysis post-treatment if hematuria persists.  
   – Treatment: as per UTI management.  
   – Referrals: consider urology referral if hematuria persists or recurs.

3. Irritable Bowel Syndrome – stable  
   – Assessment: No acute change.  
   – Treatment: Continue current Mebeverine (dose/frequency not documented); no adjustment required today.  
   – Referrals: none.

4. Recreational cannabis use (first episode)  
   – Assessment: Single recent exposure; no ongoing use.  
   – Treatment: Harm-minimisation advice; encouraged abstinence.  
   – Referrals: none.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: vital signs, physical examination, exact antibiotic and analgesic dosing, pregnancy test not performed but might be clinically relevant.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially replied “No” to sexual activity, then confirmed sexually active with long-term boyfriend – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall with minor conversational overlaps; clinically adequate.
